public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 590

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/590](https://www.erdosproblems.com/590)
 - [Ch72] Chang, C. C., A partition theorem for the complete graph on {$\omega\sp{\omega }$}. J. Combinatorial Theory Ser. A (1972), 396-452.
 - [Sp57] Specker, Ernst, Teilmengen von Mengen mit Relationen. Comment. Math. Helv. (1957), 302-314.
 - [La73] Larson, Jean A., A short proof of a partition theorem for the ordinal {$\omega \sp{\omega }$}. Ann. Math. Logic (1973/74), 129-145.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Cardinal Ordinal

namespace Erdos590

universe u

/--
Let $α$ be the infinite ordinal $\omega^{\omega}$. It was proved by Chang [Ch72] that any red/blue
colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1268917deaaaa0d674f651287027baa26cea9920/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos590.lean#L7928"]
theorem erdos_590 : OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ ω) (ω ^ ω) 3 := by
  sorry

/--
Specker [Sp57] proved that when $α=ω^2$ any red/blue
colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3]
theorem erdos_590.variants.two : OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ 2) (ω ^ 2) 3 := by
  sorry

/--
Specker [Sp57] proved that when $α=ω^n$ for $3≤ n < \omega$ then it is not the case that any
red/blue colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3]
theorem erdos_590.variants.ge_three_false {n : ℕ} (h : 3 ≤ n) :
    ¬ OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ n) (ω ^ n) 3 := by
  sorry

/--
Let m be a finite cardinal $< \omega$. Let $α$ be the infinite ordinal $\omega^{\omega}$.
It was proved by Milnor that any red/blue colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a
red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$. A shorter proof was found by Larson [La73]
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3]
theorem erdos_590.variants.finite_cardinal (m : ℕ) : OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ ω) (ω ^ ω) m := by
  sorry

end Erdos590

findings.description: The docstring describes a blue K₃, although the theorem correctly asserts a blue clique of arbitrary finite cardinality m. The introductory parameter m consequently never appears in the docstring's conclusion. The Lean statement itself matches the source.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/590: Milner's extension remains true when “we replace $K_3$ by $K_m$ for all finite $m<\omega$.”
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “a blue $K_3$” with “a blue $K_m$” in this theorem's docstring; leave the Lean statement unchanged.

findings.description: The docstring attributes the finite-cardinal extension to “Milnor,” but the cited source credits Milner. This is an attribution error, not an error in the mathematical statement.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/590: “Milner modified Chang's proof to prove that this remains true if we replace $K_3$ by $K_m$ for all finite $m<\omega$.”

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in any of the four theorem statements. Lean experiments verified the complementary-graph encoding, the inherited order-type requirement, finite cardinality semantics, natural versus ordinal powers, and the harmless m=0,1 boundary cases. Finite clique computations behaved as expected. The exact linked external proof compiled successfully; #print axioms Erdos590.erdos_590 returned only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The source's status agrees with the file. Chang's and Larson's original full texts could not be retrieved because of publisher access restrictions; their mathematical statements are explicitly recorded in the accessible problem source.
